why: The worker always needs the two largest stones, and the leftover goes back into the pile: 'repeatedly extract the max and reinsert' is exactly what a max-heap does in O(log n) per step.
hints: Each step needs the two heaviest stones from a pile that keeps changing. Sorting once is not enough, because the remainder must be put back in the right place.
Keep all weights in a max-heap. Pop two; if they differ, push the difference back. Stop when at most one stone remains.
Python heapq is a min-heap, so store negated weights. At most n - 1 smashes, each O(log n): O(n log n) total.
pitfalls: Return 0 when the heap empties, as in the example where the last two stones are both 1.
Forgetting to negate values (or negate back) when using heapq.
Re-sorting the whole list after every smash is O(n^2 log n) and times out at n = 10^5.
